Job no: 944050

Work type: Full time

Located in: Adelaide CBD

Categories: Administration, Business and Management, Human Resources and WHS, Workplace-Industrial Relations




 

Department for Health and Wellbeing - Corporate and Infrastructure - Workforce Services

Salary: $112,163 to $121,246 - ASO7 - Full Time - Ongoing - Permanent

Overview:

At DHW, we are transforming the way Human Resources partners with the business. We are evolving from a traditional HR support model to a strategic, commercially focused partnership approach, one that places business insight at the heart of people decisions while ensuring the delivery of high-quality, responsive workforce services.

As a Principal HR Business Partner, you will play a pivotal role in shaping this transformation. Working closely with Executives and Senior Leaders, you will act as a trusted strategic advisor, helping to align workforce and people strategies with organisational objectives. At the same time, you will provide leadership and oversight across key operational HR activities, ensuring workforce solutions are practical, timely and deliver measurable outcomes.

This is an opportunity to influence meaningful change, strengthen leadership capability, and enhance both organisational performance and employee experience across the organisation.

What you'll bring

Demonstrated experience delivering customer-focused HR and workforce services, balancing strategic priorities with operational excellence.

Strong business and workforce acumen, with the ability to understand operational challenges and translate them into effective people solutions.

Exceptional stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to influence, negotiate and build trusted relationships at all levels of an organisation.

Experience providing expert advice across a broad range of workforce matters, including workforce planning, organisational change, employee relations, performance, capability, and talent management.

Strong consulting and problem-solving capability, with the ability to develop tailored, innovative, and practical workforce solutions in complex environments.

Experience coaching and supporting leaders to navigate workforce challenges, build capability and achieve business outcomes.

A commitment to continuous improvement, using data, insights, and feedback to enhance HR service delivery and organisational effectiveness.

SA Health is committed to providing an inclusive workplace that embraces diversity and inclusion for all employees. We strongly encourage applications from people of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander descent, culturally diverse backgrounds, members of the LGBTIQA+SB community and people who live with disability and-or neurodivergence.

We are committed to making workplace adjustments to provide a positive and supportive work environment. You are encouraged to let us know if have any support or access requirements during the recruitment process and beyond to ensure you can perform at your best.

The South Australian public sector promotes diversity and flexible ways of working part-time. Applicants are encouraged to discuss the flexible working arrangements for this role.

Appointment will be subject to a satisfactory Criminal History Check and appropriate immunisation requirements.

Job ref: 944050

Criminal History Screening Requirement

A 'National Police Certificate' NPC (also known as a 'Nationally Coordinated Criminal History Check' NCCHC) for employment involving no contact with vulnerable groups is required for this position (general employment).

Immunisation Risk for this position is Category C (minimal patient contact).

SA Health Services are required to implement the Addressing vaccine preventable disease: Occupational assessment, screening and vaccination policy in the workplace.

Trading under Publicis Media Australia
Location: Sydney or Melbourne or Brisbane
	
Associate Strategy Manager & Strategy Manager (Also known as Associate Strategy/Planning Manager or Strategy & Planning Manager or Associate Communications Planner

This role is focused on assisting the Strategy Directors on providing the overall strategic direction for your clients.

Key Responsibilities:
•	Build strong working relationships with client, media and creative partners & Internal stakeholders
•	Apply a deep understanding of the consumer in response to all briefs
•	Translate consumer understanding into actionable, fact-based strategies
•	Translate strategies to channel 
•	Deliver innovative and proactive solutions in problem solving
•	Create the vision and strategy and then inspire others to work towards it
•	Deliver excellence in execution
•	Contribution to the company e.g. pitches, company meetings
•	Have a keen understanding of latest media and marketing trends, technology, and consumer 

Experience required: Minimum of 3 years industry experience, most recently in a similar position. Proven business acumen in medium to large agency.
Possess an expert understanding of consumer psychology, behavioural economics, macro-economic influences, trends and current marketing science thinking and an exceptional ability to make this actionable.

Salary - $80k-$100k package 


Associate Strategy Director (Also known as Associate Strategy & Planning Director or Associate Communications Planner)

The Associate Strategy Director, alongside the Strategy Director, is responsible for their teams work and output. They are responsible for ensuring work is always consumer-centric, holistic, insight-led and clearly focussed on actionable and measurable outcomes for clients.   

Key Responsibilities: 
•	Ensure media strategy recommendations deliver on the clients brief via clear and innovative media recommendations. 
•	Ensure planning recommendations deliver on communications strategy and demonstrates planning theory and rigour.  
•	Applies historical campaign learnings to define future strategic approaches. 
•	Utilises segmentation analysis to define and prioritise consumer target audiences.  
•	Ensures a thorough understanding of clients’ business and clients’ internal pressures and reflect this in client correspondence.  
•	Interrogates competitive and audience data to assist in the development of a media strategy. 
•	Collaborates with external agency partners on creative solutions.  
•	Pro-actively manages the development of media initiatives which satisfy client objectives within the given timeframes. 
•	Constantly strives to demonstrate ways to help clients achieve their business objectives, even if they’re not directly related to a current brief.  
•	Independently runs client and agency brainstorming sessions 

Experience required: Minimum 4 years industry experience, most recently in a similar position.  Proven business acumen in medium to large agency. Possess an expert understanding of consumer psychology, behavioural economics, macro-economic influences, trends and current marketing science thinking and an exceptional ability to make this actionable.

Salary - $100k-$120k package 


Strategy Director (Also known as Strategy/Planning Director or Communications Director)
The Strategy Director manages a portfolio of business within the Spark Foundry client roster. They should demonstrate leadership and inspire their team as well as client teams to deliver famously effective ideas which helps our clients grow

Key Responsibilities:
•	Responsible for the strategic output on every element of their clients business and is relentless in ensuring it meets the highest possible standards.  They will work closely with the Client/Account Director’s, to ensure that the product delivered to clients is truly integrated and best in class.
•	Participates in, embraces and lead training forums for their team and where applicable the common good of the agency.
•	Develops long-term, mutually beneficial relationships with all clients and should own the Marketing Manager and indeed in some instances the Marketing Director level client relationship.  
•	Works proactively to identify organic growth opportunities and be seen as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders within their clients business.
•	Involved in agency new business where relevant
•	Develop best in class communication strategies that deliver famously effective work. 
•	Deliver the insight and rationale to deliver the big leaps of faith clients should be taking.
•	Understand the difference you need to make for your clients at a business level not just a communications one and ensure strategic priorities are geared to business growth.
•	Identifies insights that are compelling, not naturally obvious and genuinely unlock behaviour change.
•	Ensure all media strategy recommendations deliver on the clients brief via clear and innovative media recommendations
•	Ensures planning and implementation recommendations deliver on communications strategy and that they demonstrate planning theory and rigour. 
•	Proactively strives to demonstrate ways to help clients achieve their business objectives, even if they’re not directly related to a current brief
•	Applies historical campaign learnings to define future strategic approaches.
•	Utilises segmentation analysis to define and prioritise consumer target audiences. 
•	Consistently demonstrates a thorough understanding of clients’ business and clients’ internal pressures and reflect this in client correspondence.
•	Collaborates with external agency partners on creative solutions. 
•	Helps manage, develop and lead more junior members of the team and broader agency

Experience required:  Minimum 6 years industry experience, most recently in a similar position.Proven business acumen in medium to large agency. Possess an expert understanding of consumer psychology, behavioural economics, macro-economic influences,  trends and current marketing science thinking and an exceptional ability to make this actionable.
Salary – over threshold 

•	All of the above roles require a relevant tertiary qualification or a minimum of 5 years of relevant experience in lieu of qualification.

•	Roles could also be available in Sydney, Melbourne, Brisbane

About the Position:
This full-time Retail Manager (General) role has been created to professionalise the day-to-day operations of the Subway store, reducing the current heavy reliance on the business owner. Reporting directly to the owner/franchisee, the Retail Manager will take full responsibility for leading operations, staff management, compliance, inventory, and customer service excellence. This key leadership position will enable the business to operate independently and sustainably, supporting long-term growth and allowing the owner to focus on strategic development.
Key Responsibilities:
Organise, direct and control the daily operations of the restaurant to ensure efficient and profitable performance in line with Subway franchise standards.
Manage inventory levels, purchasing, stock control, and wastage to maintain optimal product availability and quality.
Lead staff recruitment, training, rostering, supervision, and performance management to build a capable and motivated team.
Uphold exceptional customer service standards, resolve complaints promptly, and monitor feedback to drive continuous improvement.
Ensure full compliance with food safety, workplace health and safety, franchise policies, and all regulatory requirements.
Monitor sales, labour costs, and operational expenses, implementing strategies to improve profitability and efficiency.
Oversee marketing activities, promotional campaigns, and third-party delivery platforms to support business growth.
Manage operational issues, staff shortages, and day-to-day decision-making to ensure business continuity without constant owner involvement.
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply.
Minimum Diploma in Business Management, Retail Management or Hospitality Management (particularly for fast food or quick service restaurants).
Minimum 1 year in retail food management, with strong leadership and people management skills.
Demonstrated experience managing retail, fast-food, hospitality or franchise operations, including inventory control, workforce management, food safety, WHS, and compliance.
Proven ability to analyse business performance, implement operational improvements, and deliver excellent customer service.
Strong communication, organisational, problem-solving and leadership skills with the ability to foster a positive team culture.
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Target Business Services
Location: 9 Limbee Gld, Huntingdale, WA 6110
Salary: $80,000 Plus 12% Superannuation
Position: Full Time, Permanent

Our client, Khosa Concrete & Landscaping Pty Ltd, located in Huntingdale, Western Australia, is a growing construction business specialising in high-quality concreting, landscaping and outdoor construction solutions throughout the Perth metropolitan area. The company delivers a broad range of residential and commercial projects, including concrete driveways, pathways, patios, retaining walls, paving, fencing, timber structures, artificial turf installations and complete landscape transformations. 

Due to continued business growth and an increasing volume of construction projects, our client is seeking an experienced and motivated Carpenter to join its skilled construction team. The successful applicant will undertake a variety of carpentry works associated with building interiors, outdoor living spaces and structural construction, while ensuring projects are completed safely, efficiently and to the highest quality standards.

Key Responsibilities:

-	Read and interpret construction drawings, plans and specifications to determine materials, dimensions and installation requirements. 
-	Measure, cut, shape, assemble and install timber, plywood and other building materials to required specifications. 
-	Construct, install and repair timber frameworks, wall frames, floor systems, roof structures, partitions and ceilings. 
-	Install doors, windows, skirting boards, architraves, staircases, cabinetry and other interior and exterior timber fittings. 
-	Build and install pergolas, decking, fencing, gates and other outdoor timber structures. 
-	Carry out first-fix and second-fix carpentry works for residential and commercial building projects. 
-	Undertake formwork construction where required to support building and landscaping projects. 
-	Repair and maintain existing timber structures, fixtures and fittings to ensure structural integrity and appearance. 
-	Operate, maintain and inspect carpentry tools, machinery and equipment in a safe and efficient manner. 
-	Estimate material requirements and assist in ordering timber and construction materials. 
-	Ensure all carpentry works comply with Australian building codes, project specifications and workplace health and safety requirements. 
-	Liaise professionally with clients, supervisors and other trades to ensure projects are completed on time and to a high standard.

Skills & Qualifications

-	AQF Certificate III in Carpentry (or equivalent trade qualification), including at least two years of structured on-the-job training, or AQF Certificate IV in a relevant trade.
-	Minimum one year of relevant full-time experience as a Carpenter.
-	Ability to accurately read and interpret construction drawings, plans and specifications.
-	Strong knowledge of construction methods, building materials and safe work practices.
-	High attention to detail with excellent workmanship and problem-solving abilities.
-	Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment.
-	Good organisational and time management skills with the ability to meet project deadlines.
-	Sound understanding of Australian Workplace Health and Safety requirements.

Please note only shortlisted candidates will be contacted and your application will be treated as strictly confidential.
To apply for this position, email your resume to recruitment@targetbusiness.com.au
